name: Anantara The Marker Dublin
positioning: Sleek, contemporary hotel overlooking the waterfront of Grand Canal Square in Dublin's regenerated Docklands, with an infinity-pool spa and a rooftop terrace
best_for: Travelers who want a modern waterfront base in the Docklands, close to the IFSC and the Convention Centre Dublin
Guests who want a spa with an infinity pool, sauna and steam room

facts.text: The hotel overlooks the waterfront of Grand Canal Square.
The hotel is part of Dublin's regenerated Docklands.
The building is sleek and contemporary, inspired by the elements.
Conde Nast Traveler calls the building the unofficial landmark of the Docklands, known as the Silicon Docks.
The spa and wellness centre has a sauna, a jacuzzi and a eucalyptus-infused steam room.
Rooms feature pops of neon green and vivid purple.
Suites come as studios or with one or two bedrooms.
A local expert leads a storytelling tour through the historic Dublin Docklands.
Guests can learn to craft an Irish coffee guided by a local coffee master.
The hotel is within walking distance of College Green plaza and the Grafton Street shopping hub.
The hotel is close to the IFSC and the Convention Centre Dublin.
Forbes Street by Gareth Mullins serves a modern Irish menu.

highlights.text: The spa has a 23 metre infinity pool.
The Rooftop Bar & Terrace offers 360-degree views of the cityscape.
Rooms have floor-to-ceiling windows with views of Dublin and the mountains.
The rooftop hosts free yoga classes for guests.
Bathrooms are marble and stocked with Malin+Goetz toiletries.

considerations.text: The Rooftop Bar & Terrace opens only from April to September.
Parking is operated off-site with a local partner, with self-parking and valet options.
WhataHotel notes that the modern business district setting may lack traditional Dublin charm.
